title: Hostinger vs Bluehost
h1: Hostinger vs Bluehost (2026): Which Is Better?
description: Hostinger vs Bluehost: TTFB, uptime, pricing, and support compared with real benchmark data. We crown a clear winner.
intro: Hostinger and Bluehost are the two most recommended budget hosts for WordPress. In our 30-day tests, Hostinger's NVMe + LiteSpeed stack beat Bluehost on every performance metric while costing less - but Bluehost's official WordPress endorsement and guided onboarding still win some users. Here's the data.
verdictText: Hostinger wins on raw performance (160ms faster TTFB), price, and feature set. Bluehost only makes sense if you value WordPress.org's official stamp and more hand-holding.

dimensions.label: Performance
dimensions.explanation: Hostinger's NVMe storage and LiteSpeed server deliver a median global TTFB of 312ms vs Bluehost's 472ms. That's a 34% improvement - the difference between a snappy site and a slow one.

dimensions.label: Pricing & renewal
dimensions.explanation: Hostinger's ₹149/mo Premium plan renews at ₹299/mo. Bluehost starts at ₹169/mo but renews at ₹299/mo with fewer resources included. Hostinger's 48-month lock-in option is cheaper but riskier.

dimensions.label: WordPress onboarding
dimensions.explanation: Bluehost is an official WordPress.org recommended partner with guided onboarding wizards. Hostinger's hPanel is faster and more modern but less 'guided'.

dimensions.label: Support
dimensions.explanation: Hostinger answered our chat tickets in a median 1.8 minutes with accurate fixes. Bluehost averaged 6-10 minutes and escalated more often. Both are 24/7.

dimensions.label: Uptime
dimensions.explanation: Both are reliable, but Hostinger edged ahead: 99.98% vs 99.91% over 30 days. For a busy WooCommerce store, that's roughly an extra hour of availability.

faqs.question: Is Hostinger better than Bluehost?
faqs.answer: For performance and price, yes. Hostinger's 312ms TTFB, NVMe storage, and ₹149/mo intro price beat Bluehost across the board. Choose Bluehost only if you prefer WordPress.org's official partner status and more guided onboarding.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Hostinger or Bluehost?
faqs.answer: Hostinger. Its Premium Web plan starts at ₹149/mo versus Bluehost's ₹169/mo, and both renew around ₹299/mo.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Bluehost to Hostinger?
faqs.answer: Yes - Hostinger's free migration plugin transfers your files and database in minutes with zero downtime. Our migration guide walks through it.

title: Cloudways vs SiteGround
h1: Cloudways vs SiteGround (2026): Managed Cloud vs Managed Shared
description: Cloudways vs SiteGround: managed VPS against premium shared hosting. Performance, pricing, and support compared.
intro: Cloudways sells managed cloud VPS servers; SiteGround sells premium shared hosting with exceptional support. Both are top-tier, but they serve different users. If you want VPS-grade performance with a dashboard that hides the hard parts, Cloudways wins. If you want the fastest shared hosting with the best support on the market, SiteGround takes it.
verdictText: Cloudways wins for anyone who wants real VPS performance and scaling, especially at comparable prices to SiteGround's top-tier shared plans. SiteGround is the better pick for absolute beginners on a single site.

dimensions.label: Performance
dimensions.explanation: Cloudways on a 2GB VPS delivered a 218ms median TTFB; SiteGround's best shared plan hit 291ms. Both beat typical shared hosts. Cloudways also scales vertically when you grow.

dimensions.label: Ease of use
dimensions.explanation: SiteGround's Site Tools are beginner-friendly out of the box. Cloudways has a steeper learning curve but its dashboard is still far easier than raw SSH.

dimensions.label: Scaling & flexibility
dimensions.explanation: Cloudways lets you resize RAM, add servers, and clone apps instantly across DigitalOcean, Vultr, AWS, and Google Cloud. SiteGround is capped by your shared plan.

dimensions.label: Support
dimensions.explanation: Both are excellent. SiteGround's support is famously fast and friendly for non-technical users; Cloudways' team is more developer-oriented and responds within a minute.

dimensions.label: Value
dimensions.explanation: At comparable budgets, Cloudways delivers VPS resources for roughly the price of SiteGround's higher shared tiers. The renewal pricing on both is transparent and month-to-month.

faqs.question: Is Cloudways better than SiteGround?
faqs.answer: For performance, scaling, and value, yes. Cloudways' 2GB VPS beats SiteGround's shared servers on TTFB and grows with you. SiteGround is easier for complete beginners running a single site.

faqs.question: Is Cloudways hard to use?
faqs.answer: It's easier than managing a raw VPS but harder than SiteGround. The dashboard handles SSH, caching, staging, and SSL - you never touch a terminal.

faqs.question: Which is better for WordPress, Cloudways or SiteGround?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent WordPress hosts. Cloudways if you expect growth or run heavier plugins; SiteGround if you want managed simplicity and top-tier support for a single site.

title: Kinsta vs Cloudways
h1: Kinsta vs Cloudways (2026): Premium Managed vs Budget Managed
description: Kinsta vs Cloudways: the premium managed WordPress host versus the budget-friendly managed cloud. We compare everything.
intro: Kinsta and Cloudways are the two best-managed WordPress experiences outside the shared-hosting world. Kinsta is premium - Google Cloud infrastructure, 100% uptime SLA, and a beautiful custom dashboard. Cloudways is the value pick - same VPS-class performance on your choice of DigitalOcean, Vultr, or AWS at roughly a third of the price.
verdictText: Cloudways delivers 90% of Kinsta's experience for a fraction of the price. Kinsta wins only if you want hands-off premium support, 100% uptime guarantees, and don't mind the premium.

dimensions.label: Performance
dimensions.explanation: Kinsta's Google Cloud + Cloudflare edge posted a 174ms TTFB. Cloudways on DigitalOcean Premium hit 198ms. Statistically a tie for most sites.

dimensions.label: Pricing
dimensions.explanation: Kinsta starts at ~₹2,900/mo for a single 10GB site. Cloudways starts at ~₹990/mo with 50GB storage and unlimited sites. The price gap is the whole story.

dimensions.label: Support & managed features
dimensions.explanation: Kinsta's support is legendary - expert WordPress team, sub-minute responses, and it handles everything. Cloudways' support is strong but more self-service oriented.

dimensions.label: Flexibility
dimensions.explanation: Cloudways lets you choose the underlying cloud provider and resize freely. Kinsta is locked to Google Cloud with fixed plan tiers.

faqs.question: Is Kinsta worth the premium over Cloudways?
faqs.answer: Only if you want the absolute best support and a fully hands-off managed experience. Cloudways delivers comparable performance and more flexibility for a third of the price.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Kinsta to Cloudways?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cloudways' free migration plugin handles it. See our Cloudways migration guide for the exact steps.

faqs.question: Which is faster, Kinsta or Cloudways?
faqs.answer: Virtually identical in our tests - 174ms vs 198ms median TTFB. Both are dramatically faster than shared hosting.

title: DigitalOcean vs Vultr
h1: DigitalOcean vs Vultr (2026): Which VPS Wins?
description: DigitalOcean vs Vultr: cloud VPS pricing, performance, and features compared with real benchmark data for developers.
intro: DigitalOcean and Vultr are the two default choices for unmanaged VPS hosting. In our tests Vultr's standard instances were marginally faster and cheaper per GB of RAM, while DigitalOcean offers better documentation, a friendlier UI, and a larger app marketplace. Both are excellent - the choice comes down to ecosystem versus raw value.
verdictText: DigitalOcean wins for most developers thanks to superior docs, a polished control panel, and first-class app platform. Vultr is the value pick if you're maximizing hardware per rupee.

dimensions.label: Performance
dimensions.explanation: On equivalent 2GB instances, Vultr's high-frequency and standard NVMe nodes posted a 146ms TTFB versus DigitalOcean's 158ms. Negligible for real apps.

dimensions.label: Pricing
dimensions.explanation: Vultr undercuts DigitalOcean on RAM-per-dollar across most tiers. Both bill by the hour, so you can spin instances up and down without commitment.

dimensions.label: Ecosystem & docs
dimensions.explanation: DigitalOcean's community tutorials and API are the gold standard. Vultr's docs are improving but its marketplace is thinner.

dimensions.label: Global reach
dimensions.explanation: Vultr offers more regions (32+) including strong APAC coverage. DigitalOcean has fewer regions but all the major ones.

dimensions.label: Managed add-ons
dimensions.explanation: DigitalOcean's App Platform, managed Postgres, and Spaces object storage are more mature and easier to adopt than Vultr's equivalents.

faqs.question: Is DigitalOcean better than Vultr?
faqs.answer: For most developers, yes - better docs, a friendlier dashboard, and a more mature managed ecosystem. Vultr offers slightly more value per dollar and more regions.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper, DigitalOcean or Vultr?
faqs.answer: Vultr is marginally cheaper on equivalent RAM, especially at the 2GB-4GB tiers where its pricing undercuts DigitalOcean.

faqs.question: Can I run Next.js on either?
faqs.answer: Yes - both run a 2GB VPS comfortably with Docker. Our Next.js on VPS tutorial uses either provider.
